title: Manifest mismatch — partial object + recovery scratchpad
body:
Top-level problem: model load fails intermittently with 'manifest.json mismatch' during weights staging. Error only affects one customer region (eu-west-1) and happens ~1-2% of fetches. Hypothesis: object upload completed but manifest update race or partial object (range read) returning truncated blob. Could be proxy/edge caching returning older manifest or incomplete writes when using multipart uploads + rewriting manifest concurrently.

What I've seen (repro steps and logs):
1) Triggered model-version rollout to dedicated pool (small test).
2) Worker logs (abridged):
   - load_model: fetching manifest: gs://rw-models/prod/oryx-v2/12345/manifest.json
   - fetch: GET returned 200 but content-length 0 (??)
   - json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)
   - fallback: try HEAD -> HEAD ok, content-length 5843 -> subsequent GET returns partial content (truncated at ~1.9k bytes)
   - checksum mismatch: expected sha256: 8d3f... got 0000... or truncated file length

Commands I ran locally against GCS bucket: (to try reproduce / validate)
$ gsutil cp gs://rw-models/prod/oryx-v2/12345/manifest.json ./mf.json && jq . mf.json | head -n 20
$ gsutil -m stat gs://rw-models/prod/oryx-v2/12345/**
$ curl -I -L "https://storage.googleapis.com/rw-models/prod/oryx-v2/12345/manifest.json"
$ python -c 'import requests; print(requests.get("https://storage.googleapis.com/rw-models/prod/oryx-v2/12345/manifest.json").content[:200])'

Observed: sometimes gsutil cp succeeds (full size), sometimes it writes a 0-byte file locally then later the same GET returns full file. Pattern looks like transient consistency or CDN caching. But: GCS is supposed to be strongly consistent. Another angle: our asset write job does a rewrite (compose) after uploading parts; if a consumer reads during compose, might get empty or partial object. Need to verify producer flow.

Producer (deploy pipeline) details:
- Upload flow: multipart parts copied to staging-objects/ then compose to final, then write manifest.json that references new object names and their sha256.
- There is a short window between compose completing and manifest being updated/replicated to CDN. If consumer follows manifest immediately and tries to fetch parts by name, should be ok (object exists). But logs show manifest fetch failing, not parts. So maybe manifest itself is being written via rewrite and proxy caches fronting bucket return 0 length.

Other error snippet captured in SRE bucket logs:
[2024-11-08T15:42:34Z] fetch_manifest: GET /prod/oryx-v2/12345/manifest.json 200 "content-length: 0" source=gw-proxy-2
[2024-11-08T15:42:34Z] parse_manifest: json error -> EOF
[2024-11-08T15:42:34Z] retry (1/3) backoff=250ms
[2024-11-08T15:42:35Z] GET same url -> 206 bytes -> parse ok -> continue

What I tried so far (and results):
- Force read-after-write by calling GET after compose: sometimes returns full file, sometimes empty. Non-deterministic.
- Added a HEAD+If-Range style check: HEAD returns expected content-length then GET still can return partial. So HEAD not fully helpful.
- Switched to signed URL (V4) from our storage proxy and tested direct curl: still saw truncated responses from certain egress IPs (eu region).
- Tried using range requests (curl -r 0-): server returned 416 on some attempts.
- Increased client timeout & retries: mitigates but does not eliminate.
- Implemented local consumer-side guard: verify content-length == expected and sha256 matches; if not, sleep 200ms and retry 3x. This reduced incidents to ~0.2% but not zero.

New hypotheses: 
A) Edge/Proxy caching (internal CDN or GCS behind proxy) occasionally serves an empty body for freshly-written small files due to concurrent rewrite. Possibly our edge returns 200 with empty body while bucket is in internal transient state.
B) Producer race: manifest upload is done by parallel job that sometimes writes a zero-byte placeholder file before atomic write (rare bug in our uploader). Need to inspect the uploader codepath for temporary file writes.
C) Network middlebox truncating connection for small payloads during high concurrency windows (less likely).

Data to collect next:
- Correlate occurrences with deployment events (did the incidents cluster around our compose jobs?). Check ENG-4123 timeline.
- Log request IDs from GCS response headers (x-goog-request-id) when we see a 0-byte response. We currently don't capture that header in fetch logs — add it immediately.
- Collect egress IP and gw-proxy id for all failing requests. Filter by eu-west-1.
- Add checksum and content-length to the manifest object metadata (x-goog-meta-sha256) at upload time to allow HEAD verification without full GET.

Potential mitigations (short term):
- Consumer: keep the retry-with-backoff + verify-checksum guard in loader. Increase max retries and exponential backoff jitter for region eu-west-1 only.
- Producer: change uploader to perform write-to-temp-object then rewrite+delete pattern (ensure no zero-byte placeholders). If we already do this, add fsyncs or use compose with finalized objects only.
- Network: route calls to storage via alternate egress (try bypassing internal CDN) as experiment.

Actions taken / TODOs: 
- [x] Add header capture (x-goog-request-id, x-cache) to loader logs (Marcus helped PR) -> deployed to staging 2024-11-09.
- [x] Implemented SHA256 verification fallback + 3 retry loop -> deployed to staging (reduced rate).
- [ ] Audit uploader code (check for any path that does object with Content-Length: 0 write before actual content). Assigned to Anya. (ENG-4123)
- [ ] Run targeted reproduce by issuing 500 parallel GETs immediately after a known compose job in staging (Marcus).
- [ ] If reproduce succeeds, capture tcpdump at gw-proxy and compare responses.
- [ ] Add x-goog-meta-sha256 to manifest uploads (requires CI update) -> feature ticket created.

Open questions / notes:
- Why does HEAD sometimes show full content-length while GET returns partial? Is there a layer that synthesizes HEAD from metadata but proxies GET to an inconsistent replica?
- Are we using any GCS bucket-level lifecycle or rewrite rules that could transiently present an object placeholder?
- Check if any ACL rewrite or encryption (CMEK/HSM) transforms are conducted inline that could slow finalization.

Useful snippets for debugging (paste into terminal on staging access):
# capture headers and body with curl (saves headers to file)
curl -s -D headers.txt -o body.bin "https://storage.googleapis.com/rw-models/prod/oryx-v2/12345/manifest.json" || true
sha256sum body.bin; wc -c body.bin; cat headers.txt | egrep -i 'x-goog|content-length|etag|cache'

# loop to trigger high concurrency read immed after compose (be careful, spammy)
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{size_download}\n" "https://storage.googleapis.com/rw-models/prod/oryx-v2/12345/manifest.json" & done; wait

Notes-to-self: keep this doc as the canonical incident breadcrumb for ENG-4123 until resolved. If we patch uploader, rerun the reproduce test 24 hours after deploy to confirm.

If anyone reading: ping me in #eng-serving-runtime with request-id value if you hit this in prod so we can link traces. Also add any related logs to ENG-4123.
